Formulation  
Patient is a 41-year-old postpartum female, four weeks post-C-section, presenting with acute onset shortness of breath and tachycardia. The recent surgical delivery is a predisposing factor for thromboembolism. Stress and anxiety related to physical symptoms may be contributing to increased heart rate perception. Family history of clots heightens suspicion and awareness. Protective factors include patient insight and willingness to seek urgent care.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Risk of thromboembolism and associated anxiety/stress  
- Patient Goal(s): To have symptoms evaluated urgently and receive appropriate treatment if needed; reduce anxiety related to symptoms  
- Clinical Goal(s): Rule out pulmonary embolism or other complications; provide reassurance, manage anxiety  
- Actions (Patient): Attend hospital promptly for diagnostic evaluation; cease use of codeine until reviewed; monitor symptoms and report deterioration immediately  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Facilitate referral or emergency advice to hospital; educate patient on symptom monitoring; assess for anxiety and provide supportive counseling as required  

Secondary Problem: Anxiety/stress related to postnatal recovery and symptoms  
- Patient Goal(s): Achieve better stress management and emotional stability during recovery  
- Clinical Goal(s): Identify and treat anxiety if persistent after medical evaluation; consider referral for mental health support if indicated  
- Actions (Patient): Communicate feelings of anxiety and stress; engage with support networks  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Screen for anxiety postpartum during follow-up; provide psychoeducation and consider referral to counseling services if anxiety persists  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Recognition of thromboembolism symptoms, importance of urgent hospital evaluation, risks associated with C-section, cessation of codeine prior to hospital review  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increasing shortness of breath, chest pain, swelling/pain in legs, worsening tachycardia, syncope  
- Coping Strategies: Immediate help-seeking, use of social support, relaxation techniques (not specifically documented but implied need)
